title: Comparing AI Models
description: A practical side-by-side comparison of the major AI models to help you decide which to use for each task.

data.text: Rather than declaring a "best" model — which changes every few months as models improve — this lesson gives you a stable decision framework you can apply to any task to pick the right model in under 30 seconds.
The current model landscape

As of late 2026, four AI products dominate everyday knowledge work: ChatGPT (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), and Perplexity. Each is built on large language models — but they differ significantly in where they excel, how they handle long content, whether they retrieve live information, and how they integrate with other tools. Understanding these differences prevents the common mistake of force-fitting the wrong tool to a task.

data.text: One important distinction: Perplexity is not a single foundation model — it is a search-augmented interface that routes queries to underlying models (including GPT and Claude) while always retrieving live web sources. This makes it uniquely suited to factual research, even though it shares underlying model infrastructure with the others.

data.text: Model profiles: what each tool actually does well
ChatGPT — the generalist

ChatGPT is the most versatile entry point into AI. It handles writing, coding, brainstorming, translation, file analysis, image generation, and data analysis within a single interface. Its free tier is genuinely capable, and the paid tiers add code execution, file uploads, and image generation. The GPT Store lets users install community-built custom assistants for specialized tasks.

Its main limitation is that it does not cite sources by default, and web browsing is only available on paid plans. It also tends toward verbosity, which can require prompt discipline to manage. For the majority of everyday knowledge work, ChatGPT is a reliable default choice.
Claude — the careful thinker

Claude is built by Anthropic with an emphasis on helpfulness, safety, and avoiding harmful outputs. The Claude 5.5 family — Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 — offers a 1M-token context window, roughly 750,000 words, which allows it to hold an entire book, legal brief, or codebase in a single conversation. Claude tends to be more cautious and precise in its wording, making it well-suited to editing, legal or policy document review, and tasks where accuracy of nuance matters.

Claude does not generate images. Its web browsing capability is more limited than ChatGPT or Gemini. It does not have a native integration with third-party productivity suites. Where it excels: long documents, careful writing, instruction-following at scale, and tasks where you want the AI to stay precisely on-brief without improvising.
Gemini — the Google-native assistant

Gemini is Google's AI, and its primary advantage is deep integration with Google Workspace — Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, and Meet. If your work lives in these tools, Gemini can summarize email threads, draft replies, generate slide decks from a document, and analyze spreadsheets without any copy-pasting. Gemini 4 Argon (paid) offers a 1M-token context window, among the largest of any major consumer AI product, while Gemini 3.8 Flash provides a faster, cheaper option.

Outside of the Google ecosystem, Gemini is competitive but rarely the strongest choice. Its web search is native and always active, which is an advantage for currency of information. For users already paying for Google AI Pro or a Workspace plan that includes Gemini, it is often the highest-value option.
Perplexity — the research assistant

Perplexity is best understood not as a chatbot but as an AI-powered search engine. Every response retrieves live sources and cites them inline — you can click any citation to verify the original. This makes it uniquely reliable for fact-checking, research, market intelligence, and any query where the answer might have changed recently. It will not help you write a story, generate an image, or analyze a spreadsheet. But for sourced factual queries, it is more reliable than any other model in the comparison.
Head-to-head comparison
Why context window size matters

The context window is the amount of text an AI model can hold in active 'working memory' during a conversation — including your messages, its replies, and any documents you upload. When content exceeds the context window, earlier parts of the conversation effectively fall out of the model's awareness, leading to forgotten instructions and inconsistent responses.

data.text: A rough rule of thumb: 1,000 tokens ≈ 750 words ≈ about 1.5 pages. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini now hold around 1M tokens each — roughly 1,500 pages, the length of a long novel or an entire codebase. Perplexity relies on web retrieval instead of a large working context. For most everyday tasks, every model has more than enough context. The difference still matters when working with very large files, where the quality of retrieval and long-context reasoning matters more than the raw limit.

data.text: Using multiple models together

Experienced AI users rarely rely on a single model. Instead, they route different stages of a task to the model best suited for each step. This is not complicated — it just requires knowing each tool's edge.

data.caption: Example: researching and writing a report using the best model for each stage
data.definition:
flowchart TD
  A[Research topic] -->|Perplexity| B[Gather cited facts]
  B -->|Claude| C[Analyze long source documents]
  C -->|ChatGPT| D[Write and structure the draft]
  D -->|Claude| E[Edit for precision and tone]
  E -->|Gemini| F[Insert into Google Doc]
  style A fill:#f0f0f0
  style B fill:#ddf4ff
  style C fill:#d1f3d8
  style D fill:#ffe1cc
  style E fill:#d1f3d8
  style F fill:#fff8c5

data.text: The workflow above is not hypothetical — it is what a careful researcher, consultant, or analyst might do on a real deliverable. Perplexity handles sourcing, Claude handles large document synthesis, ChatGPT handles drafting, and Gemini handles final delivery into Workspace. Each model does what it is best at.
How to evaluate models yourself

Published benchmarks measure performance on standardized tests — useful signals, but they do not tell you which model works best for your specific writing style, domain, and use case. The most reliable evaluation is a personal test on a real task you care about.

data.title: A simple 3-step personal evaluation process:
items: Pick one real task you do frequently (e.g., drafting a weekly update, summarizing a document, answering a customer question).
Run the exact same prompt through ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. Save all three outputs.
Read them side-by-side and ask: which is most accurate, best-toned, and requires the least editing? That model wins for this task type.

data.text: For structured benchmarks, the LMSYS Chatbot Arena (lmarena.ai) is the most trusted community-run leaderboard. It shows blind head-to-head ratings from real users across thousands of tasks — a more honest signal than lab benchmarks designed by model creators.

data.title: Start with one paid subscription, not four
data.text: If you are new to AI tools, subscribe to one paid tier — most people start with ChatGPT Plus — and use it deeply for 30 days. You will learn your actual usage patterns before deciding whether a second subscription is worth it. Paying for all four simultaneously is rarely the right call for individual users.
Switching checklist

items: Long conversation losing track? Move the source material to Claude.
Need a verifiable fact? Check Perplexity and open the cited source.
Working inside Gmail, Docs, or Sheets? Stay in Gemini.
Need image generation or code execution? Use a paid ChatGPT plan.

data.text: Models are updated frequently. This comparison reflects general strengths. Always test the current version for your specific use case — capabilities shift significantly with each major release.

data.title: Model selection principles
points: No model is best at everything — build the reflex to choose based on task type
Your prompt quality matters more than model choice for most everyday tasks
Start with ChatGPT (free), switch to Claude for long documents or careful writing
Perplexity for any fact that needs a source; Gemini for Google Workspace
Master one tool before expanding — depth beats breadth
